beginner.stem: How many protons does a Sodium atom have? (That number is also its place on the table.)
beginner.explanation: Sodium is element 11. A neutral atom has 11 protons and 11 electrons.

beginner.stem: Which element has the symbol Na?

beginner.stem: Which block of the table contains Sodium? (Blocks are s, p, d, or f.)

beginner.stem: About how heavy is a Sodium atom, in the catalog's atomic-weight number?

beginner.stem: How many electrons sit in each shell of Sodium, from the inside out?

beginner.explanation: Sodium is drawn with 3 shells.

beginner.stem: Which of these is a listed use of Sodium?
beginner.explanation: Table salt is sodium chloride. The sodium in it has already reacted and is part of a calm crystal, not the soft metal.

beginner.stem: Which of these is a listed use of Sodium?
beginner.explanation: Older yellow street lamps were sodium vapor. In the body, sodium ions help nerve cells send signals.

beginner.explanation: Sodium hydroxide, made from salt, is used to make soap, paper, and many other chemicals. The pure metal is a starting point in some of those plants.

beginner.stem: Which history line belongs to Sodium?
options: Potash, the ash of burned plants, was an old industrial alkali.
In 1766 Henry Cavendish collected a gas from metals and acids and called it inflammable air.
Johan August Arfwedson found a new alkali in the mineral petalite in 1817, working in Berzelius’s laboratory.
beginner.explanation: Soda and salt are ancient.

beginner.stem: How does the catalog describe the discovery of Sodium?
options: Henry Cavendish collected a gas by pouring acid onto iron, zinc, and tin and catching what bubbled off.
Johan August Arfwedson analyzed petalite from Utö in 1817 and, after removing silica and alumina, was left with a sulfate that was neither sodium nor potassium.
In October 1807 Humphry Davy touched the poles of a voltaic pile to a piece of moist potash, which the current melted.
Humphry Davy had isolated potassium from molten potash with a voltaic pile.
beginner.explanation: Humphry Davy had isolated potassium from molten potash with a voltaic pile.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Sodium in this catalog?
options: Metal from a Pot of Ash
beginner.explanation: Humphry Davy had just pulled a metal from potash when he turned the same current on melted caustic soda. Another silvery substance was about to appear.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Sodium in this catalog?
options: Metal from a Pot of Ash
beginner.explanation: Egypt's old mineral soda already had a name, and Latin had kept it. The English name of the new metal came from a different word, proposed by a different man.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Sodium in this catalog?
options: Fire on a Bowl of Water

beginner.explanation: The new metal looked calm for a moment after it was cut. Water was the test that showed why it could not be stored like iron.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Sodium in this catalog?
options: Metal from a Pot of Ash
beginner.explanation: Pure sodium metal never reached the dinner table, and it was never meant to. The ion, paired with chlorine, became one of the oldest seasonings people know.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Sodium in this catalog?
options: Metal from a Pot of Ash
beginner.explanation: Potassium came first, and sodium followed within days on the same kind of apparatus. The speed of the second discovery made the first one look like a method, not a lucky melt.

beginner.explanation: That Sodium line is labelled violet.

beginner.stem: Which teaching sentence belongs to Sodium at this learning mode?

beginner.stem: Which curriculum note is written for Sodium at this depth?
options: Find Lithium (Li, Z=3) on the table and note its family (Alkali metal).
Learn Potassium: say the name, write K, find Z=19 on the table, note the family (Alkali metal), and connect it to one real use — bananas and nerve signals.
